title: Integrating with Third-Party APIs
description: Call an unreliable external API without letting its outages take down your own service.

data.text: Your checkout calls a third-party tax calculation API. Last Tuesday it returned 503s for twenty minutes, and your own API returned 500s for the same twenty minutes even though nothing was wrong on your side. The finance team also wants every tax calculation to be reproducible for audit purposes.

Treat the third party as an **untrusted dependency** and wrap it in a policy: bounded **retries with jittered backoff** for transient faults, a **circuit breaker** that fails fast once the API is clearly down, a **timeout** on every call, and a **fallback** that degrades gracefully (use the last known rate, or queue the order for later). Cache successful responses in Redis keyed on the request so audit replays do not hit the vendor. Route the calls through **API Management** or a small facade so all this lives in one place and credentials stay server-side.

data.title: Resilience pipeline with Polly
Keep vendor credentials out of the client
data.code:
<!-- APIM injects the vendor key; callers never see it -->
<policies>
  <inbound>
    <rate-limit-by-key calls="100" renewal-period="60" counter-key="@(context.Subscription.Id)" />
    <set-header name="X-Api-Key" exists-action="override">
      <value>{{third-party-tax-key}}</value>
    </set-header>
  </inbound>
  <backend>
    <forward-request timeout="3" />
    <retry condition="@(context.Response.StatusCode == 503)" count="3" interval="2" />
  </backend>
</policies>

data.text: You cannot fix someone else's service, but you can decide what your own service does when it misbehaves. Retries absorb blips, a circuit breaker prevents a stampede of doomed calls from consuming your own worker threads, timeouts stop a hung vendor from exhausting your connection pool, and a fallback keeps the core user journey working. All four together are what turns "the vendor was down and so were we" into "tax was estimated and reconciled later".

cards.title: Retry + circuit breaker + fallback
pros: Fails fast when the vendor is down
cons: Fallback logic must be written per use case
Cached data may be briefly stale

cards.title: Asynchronous queue decoupling
pros: Vendor outage is invisible to users
cons: Only works when a delayed result is acceptable

cards.title: Direct synchronous call
cards.description: Call the vendor inline, no policy
